# Matt King

> Matt King is a global sports marketing leader. As Global Marketing Manager for Football at DAZN, he leads marketing across eight football rights portfolios, including the FIFA World Cup, the UEFA Champions League, Serie A, LaLiga and the Bundesliga, in seven market zones. His work takes sport off the pitch and into culture.

Matt King is a global sports marketing leader. As Global Marketing Manager for Football at DAZN, he leads marketing across eight football rights portfolios, including the FIFA World Cup, the UEFA Champions League, Serie A, LaLiga and the Bundesliga, in seven market zones, and brought more than three million FIFA+ fans onto DAZN. Before DAZN he co-founded 80 Four, a sport, health and lifestyle marketing agency named a finalist for Circle Networks Start Up of the Year, and grew brands including The Couture Club, American Golf and Gym King through partnerships with Phil Foden, Molly-Mae Hague, Niall Horan and Judy Murray. His work takes sport off the pitch and into culture: reaching new fans through the music, fashion and creators they already love. He is based between London and Manchester, and studied at Webber International University in Florida, where he played college soccer.

## Ideas
- [Dormant demand](https://www.bymattking.com/thinking/dormant-demand/): Dormant demand is passion that's fully formed but has never been given a product: fans who already care, waiting for something to watch, buy or join.
- [The side door](https://www.bymattking.com/thinking/the-side-door/): The side door is reaching new fans through what they already love, like music, fashion and creators, and then putting the sport in that world.
- [Idols sell, influencers inform](https://www.bymattking.com/thinking/idols-sell-influencers-inform/): Influencers tell people a product exists. Idols make people want to be part of it. If you need people to buy, cast an idol.

## Writing
- [Man City put a fashion label on the pitch](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/man-city-cp-company-kit/) (2026-11-26, Culture): City walked out in the Champions League in an orange kit made with C.P. Company. Here's why the smartest fashion launch of the week happened during a football match.
- [Sporting showed Manchester United who made their heroes](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/sporting-1906-tifo/) (2026-11-26, Sport): Before kick-off in Lisbon, Sporting's fans unveiled a display for the club's 120th year with a young Cristiano Ronaldo at its centre. Here's how a selling club turns the players it lost into its proudest story.
- [PSG launched a shirt in Abidjan, Dakar and Casablanca](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/psg-jordan-third-kit/) (2026-11-26, Marketing): Paris Saint-Germain and Jordan Brand took their new third kit on a journey through three African cities before bringing it home to Paris. Here's why going to where your fans are beats waiting for them to come to you.
- [Man City sang for the player in the other shirt](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/de-bruyne-etihad-return/) (2026-11-25, Sport): Kevin De Bruyne walked out at the Etihad in a Napoli shirt, and the home fans sang his song. Here's why the way a club treats its former stars is some of the best marketing it will ever do.
- [F1 just signed Nike. It wants to be worn, not just watched.](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/f1-nike/) (2026-11-23, Sport): Formula 1 has made Nike its official apparel partner from 2027, and dropped the first collection the same day in Las Vegas. Here's why the biggest move in F1 this year isn't on the track.
- [Everton put a Football Manager fan in their real press room](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/everton-football-manager-press-room/) (2026-11-22, Marketing): A fan held a pretend Everton press conference in his bedroom and went viral. Everton gave him the real room, and the real captain. Here's why the best club content this month cost almost nothing.
- [The Miami Heat become Vice City](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/miami-heat-vice-city/) (2026-11-19, Sport): The night before GTA VI launched, the Heat turned their arena into Vice City: the court, the shirts, even the burgers. Here's why borrowing the year's biggest culture moment beats fighting it.
- [Central Cee, GTA VI and the song you have to find](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/central-cee-gta-vi/) (2026-11-18, Culture): GTA VI is here, and Central Cee has a new song on its radio that isn't out anywhere else. No countdown, no big announcement. Just a track waiting for fans to find it. Here's why that's such a smart play.
- [The clipping economy](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/the-clipping-economy/) (2026-11-18, Marketing): Most people never see a full match. They see a clip, cut by someone else and posted somewhere else. Here's what sport can learn from the streamers who built a business on that.
- [Taylor Swift, the Chiefs and the side door](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/taylor-swift-chiefs/) (2026-11-18, Culture): There was no campaign. Taylor Swift went to watch Travis Kelce, and a whole new audience followed her into the NFL. Here's why it worked, and what to steal from it.
- [What Drive to Survive got right](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/drive-to-survive/) (2026-11-18, Sport): Formula 1 didn't win new fans by selling races. It let Netflix sell the people. Here's why it worked, and what every sport can steal from it.
- [Baller League and the new format](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/baller-league/) (2026-11-18, Sport): Baller League didn't ask young fans to sit through 90 minutes. It rebuilt football around how they already watch. Here's why the format is the product.
- [Alcaraz, Travis Scott and the drop](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/alcaraz-travis-scott-nike/) (2026-11-18, Culture): When tennis's biggest young star previewed Travis Scott's Nike tennis shoe, the sport turned up somewhere it rarely goes: sneaker culture. Here's why that matters.
- [AI is the pit crew, not the driver](https://www.bymattking.com/writing/ai-is-the-pit-crew/) (2026-11-18, Marketing): AI changes the tyres fast. It doesn't drive the car. How I use it in sports marketing, what it can't do yet, and why effort isn't the same as authenticity.
